verdicts.quote: “Pass the PAT as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. This method does not require an API key:”
verdicts.reason: Datadog supports first‑class, scoped Personal Access Tokens that authenticate via Bearer; this is the most suitable multi‑tenant option since public OAuth is partner‑gated.

verdicts.quote: “The Free tier includes up to 40K LLM spans per month with 15-day retention — no credit card required.”
verdicts.reason: Datadog offers a self‑serve signup with a 14‑day trial and a continuing Free tier, so developers can obtain working credentials without sales.

verdicts.quote: “endpoints, schemas, request and response examples for managing dashboards, monitors, logs, metrics, and more.”
verdicts.reason: The API covers many product areas (dashboards, monitors, logs, metrics, incidents, etc.), meeting the “broad” definition.

verdicts.quote: “The Datadog MCP Server acts as a bridge between your observability data in Datadog and any AI agents that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP).”
verdicts.reason: Datadog publishes and documents its own MCP server, indicating it is vendor‑maintained.

verdicts.quote: “OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.”
verdicts.reason: You can ship now using PATs or API/app keys, but on‑behalf‑of OAuth for a public connector requires joining the partner program, so there’s a partnership caveat.
